questions.stem: A device contains a coil rotating in a magnetic field. The coil is connected to the external circuit via slip rings. Which device is this?
questions.explanation: Slip rings are the key identifier. An AC generator uses slip rings to maintain continuous contact with the rotating coil, preserving the alternating nature of the output. A DC motor and DC generator use a split-ring commutator instead. A transformer has no rotating parts -- it uses two stationary coils on an iron core.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices uses the motor effect (current + field = force)?
questions.explanation: A loudspeaker uses the motor effect: a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a force that moves the speaker cone. A bicycle dynamo (A) and a dynamic microphone (B) both use electromagnetic induction (changing flux induces a voltage). A transformer (C) also uses electromagnetic induction -- a changing current in the primary creates a changing magnetic field that induces a voltage in the secondary.

questions.stem: A transformer has 500 turns on the primary coil and 50 turns on the secondary coil. The primary voltage is 230 V and the primary current is 0.5 A. Assuming the transformer is ideal, what is the secondary current?
questions.explanation: First find the secondary voltage: Vs = Vp x Ns/Np = 230 x 50/500 = 23 V. For an ideal transformer, power in = power out: VpIp = VsIs, so Is = VpIp/Vs = (230 x 0.5)/23 = 5 A. The voltage is stepped down by a factor of 10, so the current is stepped up by a factor of 10. This conserves energy.

questions.stem: Fleming's left-hand rule is used for the motor effect, while Fleming's right-hand rule is used for the generator effect. Which statement correctly links the rules to real devices?

options.text: Left-hand rule for generators; right-hand rule for motors
Left-hand rule for motors and speakers; right-hand rule for generators and microphones
Left-hand rule for all electromagnetic devices
Right-hand rule for all electromagnetic devices

questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule applies to the motor effect (force on a current-carrying conductor in a field), which is used in motors and speakers. Fleming's right-hand rule applies to the generator effect (electromagnetic induction), used in generators and dynamic microphones. Option A has the rules backwards. Using only one rule for all devices (C or D) fails to distinguish between the two fundamental effects.

questions.stem: A wire of length 0.15 m carries a current of 4 A perpendicular to a magnetic field. The force on the wire is 0.3 N. What is the magnetic flux density (field strength)?
questions.explanation: Rearranging F = BIL to find B: B = F/(IL) = 0.3/(4 x 0.15) = 0.3/0.6 = 0.5 T. Option A multiplies F x L/I. Option C divides F by L only. Option D multiplies F by I and L instead of dividing. Always check units: force in N, current in A, length in m gives field strength in T.
